**Dara Grace Torres** (born April 15, 1967) is an American former competitive [swimmer](/wiki/Swimming_(sport) "Swimming (sport)"), coach, and author who is a 12-time Olympic medalist and former world record-holder in three events. Torres is the first swimmer to represent the United States in five [Olympic Games](/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") (1984, 1988, 1992, 2000 and 2008), and at age 41, the oldest swimmer to earn a place on the U.S. Olympic team. At the [2008 Summer Olympics](/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics"), she competed in the 50-meter [freestyle](/wiki/Freestyle_swimming "Freestyle swimming"), 4×100-meter [medley relay](/wiki/Medley_swimming "Medley swimming"), and 4×100-meter freestyle relay, and won [silver medals](/wiki/Silver_medal "Silver medal") in all three events.

Torres won 12 Olympic medals (four gold, four silver, four bronze), at the time this was the most Olympic women's swimming medals, tied with fellow American [Jenny Thompson](/wiki/Jenny_Thompson "Jenny Thompson"). Torres won five medals at the [2000 Summer Olympics](/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics"), when at age 33, she was the oldest member of the 2000 U.S. Olympic swim team. She won at least one medal in each of the five Olympics in which she competed.

Torres is currently the Head Coach of Boston College, and will be the Head Coach of the Maccabi USA U17 Swimming national team, for the 2026 [Maccabiah Games](/wiki/Maccabiah_Games "Maccabiah Games").[[1]](#cite_note-:0-1)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/Papa_Leone_XIV_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Papa_Leone_XIV_%28cropped%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Papa_Leone_XIV_(cropped).jpg)

[Pope Leo XIV](/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV "Pope Leo XIV"), 2025

The government of Vatican City has a unique structure. As governed by the Holy See, the pope is the sovereign of the state, but he is supported by different bodies. Legislative authority is managed, in the pope's name, by the [Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State](/wiki/Pontifical_Commission_for_Vatican_City_State "Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State"), a body of cardinals appointed by the pope for five-year periods. Executive power is exercised by the [president of that commission](/wiki/President_of_the_Pontifical_Commission_for_Vatican_City_State "President of the Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State"), who is consequently also the president of the governorate, assisted by the general secretary and the deputy general secretary.[[71]](#cite_note-83)[[72]](#cite_note-84) The state's foreign relations are entrusted to the Holy See's [Secretariat of State](/wiki/Secretariat_of_State_(Holy_See) "Secretariat of State (Holy See)") and diplomatic service.

Nevertheless, the pope has absolute power in the executive, legislative, and judicial branches over Vatican City,[[73]](#cite_note-Vatican_City-85)
and is thus the only [absolute monarch](/wiki/Absolute_monarchy "Absolute monarchy") in Europe.[[74]](#cite_note-86)

Operationally, there are departments that deal with health, security, telecommunications and other matters.[[73]](#cite_note-Vatican_City-85)
